smell_validity.evidence: Broker genuinely absorbs two subsystems: judge management (class-level pools, events, verification, random selection) and the checking pipeline down to block parsing, decompression and anonymity grading, while judge and checker modules are reduced to record and plan shells. Byte-level parsing beside queue bookkeeping on the public facade makes both the fault and the healthy boundary unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every seam feature now edits one ~1000-line facade; Judge and Checker names promise behavior they no longer own, so routine work lands in the wrong place. The facade also mutates the plan's private flags, holds a duplicated raw judge list, and carries process-wide judge state on the public class. Repair restores two whole subsystem boundaries.

development_plausibility.evidence: The injected code is the project's own logic relocated nearly verbatim — same log messages, warning texts, comments and import habits — threaded through self with consistent renames. The shells retain believable compatibility reasons (deprecated subclass untouched), and new docstrings read naturally. No scaffolding or artificial regularity distinguishes it from committed accretion.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt scopes the finished state as three owners with enumerated responsibilities, forbids the stored-field reach-through near-miss, demands auditing every shipped module so absorbed logic cannot survive, and pins exact behavior: queue sentinel, warnings, stats, retries, shared-per-run yet refreshed-per-search judge semantics. It decisively blocks wrong direction, partial cleanup and over-redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct purposes need distinct decisions: judge provisioning (defaults, timeout/ssl stamping), verification and availability (class-shared pools, per-run reset, event handshake, external-IP wiring), the engine (resolver ownership, retry policy), byte-level helpers (signature threading), facade rewiring (reset and scheduling order). One resolver serves both judge resolution and DNSBL; no decision repeats.

localization_burden.evidence: Scope is narrated, not listed. Deciding each member's fate combines class-level event handshakes (set during verification, awaited per check) with config-derived flags and a runtime-pruned negotiator set driving dispatch across broker, plan, judge records and resolver. Aliases mislead: self._judges holds three roles; _judges_resolver also serves DNSBL. The deprecated subclass and queue callbacks look fixable but must stay.

repair_coordination.evidence: Interacting rules: judge state must stay process-shared yet be reset per run, while engine waits depend on those events and on verifier-mutated plan flags. A partial repair restoring construction-time clearing passes single runs but across sequential searches or concurrent appends yields stale or wiped availability; making events per-instance hangs waiting checks.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Uniform options examined: moving everything to Checker recreates the god class and leaves judge management homeless; engine-only relocation with a plan-field rewrite still lacks uniform targets for pools, events, resolver and external IP; module-function extraction leaves class state, defaults and reset ordering facade-coupled. Differing owners and lifetimes keep any single rule under 20% of ~20 locations.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Misplacing the per-run reset, or making availability per-instance, passes ordinary single-run flows but reuses stale judges on a second search in one process; judge-less schemes can also leave waits hanging. These are silent state-dependent failures, but the supplied material shows no evidence they escape existing checks, so level 4 is not established.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
